verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. Both sides assert the same disjointness of the two lifted enlarged rectangles, but the Lean states it under a weaker hypothesis than the paper's. Paper: γ ≠ γ' and K_γ ∩ K_{γ'} ≠ ∅. Lean: SlotColoring.Adj D L M (SlotColoring.lean:116), i.e. 1 ≤ L.1, 1 ≤ M.1, L ≠ M, |L.1 − M.1| ≤ 4, and (physicalBox D L ∩ physicalBox D M).Nonempty — exactly the enlarged-box interaction graph the paper builds in Step 1 of the proof ('enlarged slow boxes intersect … band indices differ by at most four'). Recovery of (6.13) as written: if the slow supports meet at a point with q > 0 then both physical masks are nonzero (or both closed windows contain) that point, so closedWindow_adjacency / masks_force_adjacency give Adj D L M, and the Lean conclusion then applies; so the Lean implies the paper's implication for every pair with 1 ≤ level, which covers Γ = {(ℓ,a,σ) : ℓ ≥ ℓ₀} of (6.8) since ℓ₀ is chosen large. The converse fails (Adj can hold when the K's do not meet), so the Lean conclusion is strictly more general. Two encoding points, both matching: the paper's R^+_γ is open (|ξ|,|η| < 2r₀) and (6.13) takes closures, while orientedRectangle is the closed rectangle |ξ|,|η| ≤ 2r — the closure; and liftedSupport of that compact rectangle is the locally finite lattice union π_{i(ℓ)}^{-1}(closure R^+_γ) = closure of R^{abs,+}_γ. The radius is a single field of SlotSystem, independent of the label and of the band, as the paper requires; the centers slotCenter h L depend on L only through its colour, which is consistent since Adj-related labels get different colours (SlotColoring.color_proper, SlotColoring.lean:185).
